metadata.title: Four proofs of the directed Brooks' Theorem

nodes.name: $k$-colouring and chromatic number
nodes.statement: A \emph{$k$-colouring} of an undirected graph $G$ is a partition $V_1, \dots, V_k$ of $V(G)$ into $k$ independent sets. The \emph{chromatic number} $\chi(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ admits a $k$-colouring.

nodes.name: Digon and acyclic digraph
nodes.statement: Digraphs in this paper have no loops or parallel arcs but allow cycles of length $2$ (\emph{digons}). A digraph is \emph{acyclic} if it contains no directed cycle.

nodes.name: Acyclic colouring (dicolouring) and dichromatic number
nodes.statement: An \emph{acyclic colouring} (or \emph{dicolouring}) of a digraph $G$ is a colouring of $V(G)$ such that no directed cycle is monochromatic. The \emph{dichromatic number} $\vec{\chi}(G)$ is the minimum number of colours in an acyclic colouring of $G$.

nodes.name: Symmetric digraph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$
nodes.statement: Given an undirected graph $G$, the \emph{symmetric digraph} $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ is obtained from $G$ by replacing each edge with a digon. Then $\chi(G) = \vec{\chi}(\overleftrightarrow{G})$.

nodes.name: Maxdegree and mindegree
nodes.statement: For a vertex $v$ of a digraph $G$: $d_{max}(v)= \max(d^+(v), d^-(v))$ and $d_{min}(v)= \min(d^+(v), d^-(v))$. Then $\Delta_{max}(G)= \max_{v}(d_{max}(v))$ and $\Delta_{min}(G)= \max_{v}(d_{min}(v))$.

nodes.name: Symmetric cycle and symmetric complete graph
nodes.statement: A \emph{symmetric cycle} (resp. \emph{symmetric complete graph}) is the digraph obtained from a cycle (resp. a complete graph) by replacing each edge with a digon.

nodes.name: Exception families $\mathcal{B}_k$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{B}_1$ is the set of directed cycles, $\mathcal{B}_2$ the set of symmetric odd cycles, and for $k \geq 3$, $\mathcal{B}_k = \{\overleftrightarrow{K}_{k+1}\}$. Members of $\mathcal{B}_k$ are called \emph{exceptions}.

nodes.name: Greedy colouring of a digraph
nodes.statement: Given a digraph $G$ and an ordering $(v_1, \dots, v_n)$ of its vertices, to \emph{colour greedily} is to colour $v_1, \dots, v_n$ in order, giving $v_i$ the minimum of the smallest colour not used in $N^+(v_i) \cap \{v_1, \dots, v_{i-1}\}$ and the smallest colour not used in $N^-(v_i) \cap \{v_1, \dots, v_{i-1}\}$.

nodes.name: $k$-regular digraph and underlying graph
nodes.statement: A digraph is \emph{$k$-regular} if every vertex satisfies $d^+(v)=d^-(v)=k$. The \emph{underlying graph} $\tilde{G}$ of $G$ is the undirected graph obtained by ignoring arc directions; $G$ is \emph{connected} iff $\tilde{G}$ is connected.

nodes.name: Direct and cyclic composition of digraphs
nodes.statement: $G$ is a \emph{direct composition} of $G_1, G_2$ on $v_1 \in V(G_1), v_2 \in V(G_2)$ if obtained from disjoint union by adding exactly one arc between $v_1, v_2$. $G$ is a \emph{cyclic composition} of $G_1, \dots, G_\ell$ if obtained by adding arcs $v_iv_{i+1}$ for $i=1,\dots,\ell-1$ and $v_\ell v_1$.

nodes.name: $k$-tree
nodes.statement: A digraph $G$ is a \emph{$k$-tree} if $\Delta_{max}(G) \leq k$ and it is constructed as: (i) members of $\mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ are $k$-trees; (ii) any direct or cyclic composition of $k$-trees is a $k$-tree.

nodes.name: Direct $k$-leaf, cyclic $k$-leaf, $k$-leaf, $k$-path
nodes.statement: A \emph{direct $k$-leaf} of $G$ is an induced $T \in \mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ such that $G$ is a direct composition of $T$ and $G-T$. A \emph{cyclic $k$-leaf} is built from $\ell \geq 1$ disjoint $T_1,\dots,T_\ell \in \mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ joined by $\ell-1$ arcs $v_iv_{i+1}$, with $G$ a cyclic composition of $G-T$ and the $T_i$. A \emph{$k$-leaf} is either type, or $G$ itself when $G \in \mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ or is a cyclic composition of members of $\mathcal{B}_{k-1}$. A \emph{$k$-path} is a disjoint union of $\ell \geq 2$ members of $\mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ joined by $\ell-1$ arcs $v_iv_{i+1}$.

nodes.name: $r$-special digraph
nodes.statement: A digraph $G$ is \emph{$r$-special} if for every vertex $v \in V(G)$, either $d_{min}(v) < r$ or $d_{min}(v) = d_{max}(v) = r$.

nodes.name: $(r_1, r_2)$-normal partition
nodes.statement: Given positive integers $r_1, r_2$, a partition $\mathcal{P} = (V_1, V_2)$ of $V(G)$ is \emph{$(r_1, r_2)$-normal} if it minimises $r_2|A(G[V_1])| + r_1|A(G[V_2])|$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{P}$-component, obstruction, $\mathcal{P}$-acceptable path, vertex move
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}$-components of $G$ are connected components of $G[V_1]$ and $G[V_2]$. A $\mathcal{P}$-component is an \emph{obstruction} if it is in $\mathcal{B}_{r_1}$ in $G[V_1]$ or $\mathcal{B}_{r_2}$ in $G[V_2]$. A path $v_1\dots v_k$ in $\tilde{G}$ is \emph{$\mathcal{P}$-acceptable} if $v_1$ is in an obstruction and the vertices lie in pairwise distinct $\mathcal{P}$-components; \emph{maximal} if every neighbour of $v_k$ is in the same $\mathcal{P}$-component as some path vertex. To \emph{move} a vertex is to switch it to the other part.

nodes.name: Brooks' Theorem (undirected, cited)
nodes.statement: A connected graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G) = \Delta(G) + 1$ if and only if $G$ is an odd cycle or a complete graph.
conclusions: $\chi(G) = \Delta(G)+1$ iff $G$ is an odd cycle or a complete graph

nodes.name: Directed Brooks' Theorem (main result)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected digraph. Then $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq \Delta_{max}(G) + 1$, and equality holds iff $G$ is (a) a directed cycle, (b) a symmetric cycle of odd length, or (c) a symmetric complete graph on $\geq 4$ vertices.

nodes.name: Non-regular bound (lem:reg)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a connected non-regular digraph, then $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq \Delta_{max}(G)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma lem:reg
nodes.statement: Pick $u_1$ with $d_{min}(u_1) < \Delta_{max}(G)$; take a BFS ordering of $\tilde{G}$ from $u_1$ and greedily colour in reverse order using $\Delta_{max}(G)$ colours.

nodes.name: Directed Brooks via Lov\'asz' greedy proof
nodes.statement: A connected digraph $G$ has $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq \Delta_{max}(G)+1$ and equality holds iff $G \in \mathcal{B}_{\Delta_{max}(G)}$.

nodes.name: Lov\'asz greedy proof of directed Brooks
nodes.statement: Take a minimum counterexample $G$ which is $k$-regular with $k=\Delta_{max}(G)$. Establish four structural claims (2-connectedness, no 2-edge-cut, every 2-cut is stable, two common-neighbours form a digon or a cutset), then derive a contradiction by analysing $G-v$ for an asymmetric arc $uv$.

nodes.name: $\tilde{G}$ is 2-connected
nodes.statement: In any minimum $k$-regular counterexample $G$, the underlying graph $\tilde{G}$ is 2-connected.

nodes.name: No edge-cut of size 2
nodes.statement: $\tilde{G}$ has no edge-cut of size $2$.

nodes.name: Every 2-cut is a stable set
nodes.statement: If $\{u,v\} \subseteq V(G)$ is a cutset of $\tilde{G}$, then $\{u,v\}$ is a stable set.

nodes.name: Two same-side neighbours form a digon or cutset (Lov\'asz' claim)
nodes.statement: If $u, v$ are two out-neighbours (or two in-neighbours) of a vertex $x$, then either $\{u,v\}$ induces a digon or $\{u,v\}$ is a cutset of $\tilde{G}$.

nodes.name: Neighbours of $u$ are paired with $v$ in cutsets
nodes.statement: For every $a \in N^+(u) \setminus \{v\}$ (where $uv \in A(G)$ and $vu \notin A(G)$), the set $\{a, v\}$ is a cutset of $\tilde{G}$.

nodes.name: Directed Brooks via maximal acyclic subdigraph and induction (Rabern-style)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a digraph with $\vec{\chi}(G) = \Delta_{max}(G)+1$, then $G$ contains a connected component isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{B}_{\Delta_{max}(G)}$.

nodes.name: Proof via maximal acyclic subdigraph
nodes.statement: Take a minimum counterexample $G$ that is $k$-regular. Choose a maximal induced acyclic subdigraph $M$; then $G-M$ has $\Delta_{max} \leq k-1$ and $\vec{\chi}(G-M)=k$, so by induction it contains some $T \cong B \in \mathcal{B}_{k-1}$, and we extend a $k$-dicolouring of $G-T$ to $T$.

nodes.name: $G$ contains no $\overleftrightarrow{K}_{k+1}$ minus arc/digon ($k \geq 3$)
nodes.statement: If $k \geq 3$, the minimum counterexample $G$ cannot contain $\overleftrightarrow{K}_{k+1}$ less an arc, or less a digon, as an induced subdigraph.

nodes.name: $G$ contains no symmetric odd cycle minus arc/digon ($k=2$)
nodes.statement: If $k = 2$, the minimum counterexample $G$ cannot contain a symmetric odd cycle less an arc, or less a digon, as an induced subdigraph.

nodes.name: Mindegree of $k$-trees (Observation 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a $k$-tree. Then every vertex has mindegree at least $k-1$, and $G$ has at least $k+1$ vertices of mindegree $k-1$, except if $G = \overleftrightarrow{K}_k$ or $G$ is a symmetric path of odd length (so $k=2$).
conclusions: all vertices of $G$ have mindegree $\geq k-1$
$G$ has $\geq k+1$ vertices of mindegree $k-1$ unless $G=\overleftrightarrow{K}_k$ or a symmetric odd path

nodes.name: $k$-tree trichotomy (lem:ktree)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected digraph and $k = \Delta_{max}(G) \geq 2$. Then either $G \in \mathcal{B}_k$, or $G$ is a $k$-tree, or there exists $v \in V(G)$ with $d_{max}(v) = k$ such that no connected component of $G - \{v\}$ is a $k$-tree.
conclusions: $G \in \mathcal{B}_k$, OR $G$ is a $k$-tree, OR $\exists v$ with $d_{max}(v)=k$ and no component of $G-v$ is a $k$-tree

nodes.name: Proof of $k$-tree trichotomy
nodes.statement: Show first that $G$ has no $k$-leaf; then introduce special vertices (in some $\mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ subdigraph with maxdegree $k$) and analyse $H_v$ to either recover the desired $v$ or force $G \in \mathcal{B}_k$.

nodes.name: $G$ has no $k$-leaf (clm:no_leaf)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is connected, $\Delta_{max}(G)=k$, $G \notin \mathcal{B}_k$ and $G$ is not a $k$-tree, then $G$ has no $k$-leaf.

nodes.name: Directed Brooks via $k$-trees (Tverberg-style)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected digraph with $\Delta_{max}(G) = k$. Then $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq k+1$ and equality holds iff $G \in \mathcal{B}_k$.

nodes.name: Proof via $k$-tree trichotomy
nodes.statement: By induction on $k$: $k$-trees are $k$-dicolourable since $\mathcal{B}_{k-1}$ members are and compositions preserve it. Otherwise apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ktree} iteratively to extract an acyclic vertex set whose removal leaves $(k-1)$-dicolourable subgraphs.

nodes.name: Special-partition observation (obs:special)
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{P}$ is an $(r_1, r_2)$-normal partition of $G$ with $r_1 + r_2 \geq \Delta_{max}(G) \geq 1$, then $G[V_1]$ is $r_1$-special and $G[V_2]$ is $r_2$-special.

nodes.name: Proof of obs:special
nodes.statement: Suppose $G[V_1]$ is not $r_1$-special; pick $v_1$ violating, swap to $V_2$, and verify the partition strictly improves the normality objective $r_2|A(G[V_1])|+r_1|A(G[V_2])|$.

nodes.name: Existence of obstruction-free normal partition (lem:partition)
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq 2$. Let $G$ be a $k$-regular connected digraph with $G \notin \mathcal{B}_k$, and $r_1, r_2 \geq 1$ with $r_1+r_2=k$. Then there exists an $(r_1, r_2)$-normal partition $(V_1, V_2)$ such that $G[V_i]$ is $r_i$-special and has no obstruction for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Proof of lem:partition
nodes.statement: Among $(r_1,r_2)$-normal partitions with the minimum number of obstructions, take $\mathcal{P}$ minimising the length of a maximal $\mathcal{P}$-acceptable path; analyse $|X|=|N_A(v_\ell)|=0,\geq 2,1$ and derive a contradiction in each case.

nodes.name: Case $X = \emptyset$
nodes.statement: If $|X|=0$, moving $v_1$ creates a new $(r_1,r_2)$-normal partition $\mathcal{P}'$ for which $v_2v_3\dots v_\ell$ is a maximal $\mathcal{P}'$-acceptable path, contradicting minimality of $\ell$. Hence $|X| \geq 1$.

nodes.name: Case $|X| \geq 2$ forces $G = \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k+1}$
nodes.statement: Show $G[X \cup v_\ell]$, $G[A \cup v_\ell]$, $G[B]$ and $G[A \cup B]$ are symmetric complete digraphs by repeatedly moving vertices and using regularity of obstructions, yielding $G = \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k+1} \in \mathcal{B}_k$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Case $|X|=1$, $X=\{v_1\}$
nodes.statement: Then $\ell = 2$; after moving $v_1, v_2$, $v_2$ is alone in its component and cannot lie in any obstruction, contradiction.

nodes.name: Case $|X|=1$, $X=\{x\} \neq \{v_1\}$ forces $G$ a symmetric odd cycle
nodes.statement: Move $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_\ell$ in turn to show each $A=\{x,v_1\}$ is a digon, $r_1 = r_2 = 1$, and consecutive $v_iv_{i+1}$ are linked by digons, producing a symmetric odd cycle $v_1v_2\dots v_\ell x v_1$, so $G \in \mathcal{B}_2$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Directed Brooks via partitioned dicolouring
nodes.statement: A connected digraph $G$ has $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq \Delta_{max}(G)+1$ and equality holds iff $G \in \mathcal{B}_{\Delta_{max}(G)}$.

nodes.name: Proof via partitioned dicolouring
nodes.statement: By induction on $\Delta_{max}$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:partition} with $(r_1,r_2)=(1,k-1)$: $G_1=G[V_1]$ is acyclic and $G_2=G[V_2]$ is $(k-1)$-dicolourable (by handling vertices of maxdegree $k$ via greedy extension); use one extra colour for $V_1$.

nodes.name: $k$-\textsc{dicolourability}
nodes.statement: Input: a digraph $G$. Question: is $G$ $k$-dicolourable? Known to be NP-complete for all $k \geq 2$ (Bokal et al.\ [Bo04]).

nodes.name: NP-completeness of $k$-dicolourability with $\Delta_{min}=k$
nodes.statement: For all $k \geq 2$, $k$-\textsc{dicolourability} is $NP$-complete even when restricted to digraphs $G$ with $\Delta_{min}(G) = k$.

nodes.name: Proof of NP-completeness via gadget reduction
nodes.statement: Reduce from $k$-\textsc{dicolourability}: given $G$, build $G'$ by replacing each vertex $u$ with a gadget on $\{u^-,u^+,u_1,\dots,u_{k-1}\}$ and arcs $u^+v^-$ for each $uv \in A(G)$; show $\Delta_{min}(G') \leq k$ and $G$ is $k$-dicolourable iff $G'$ is.

nodes.name: Construct gadget digraph $G'$
nodes.statement: For each vertex $u \in V(G)$ add $k+1$ new vertices $u^-, u^+, u_1, \dots, u_{k-1}$ to $G'$. Make $G'[\{u^-, u_1,\dots,u_{k-1}\}]$ and $G'[\{u^+, u_1,\dots,u_{k-1}\}]$ symmetric complete digraphs and add the arc $u^-u^+$. For each $uv \in A(G)$, add $u^+v^- \in A(G')$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Delta_{min}(G') \leq k$
nodes.statement: Verify $d^-_{G'}(u^+) = d^+_{G'}(u^-) = k$ and $d^+_{G'}(u_i) = k$ for $i=1,\dots,k-1$, hence $\Delta_{min}(G') \leq k$.

nodes.name: $G$ $k$-dicolourable $\Rightarrow$ $G'$ $k$-dicolourable
nodes.statement: Given $\phi$ a $k$-dicolouring of $G$, colour $u^-$ and $u^+$ with $\phi(u)$ and assign the remaining $k-1$ colours bijectively to $u_1,\dots,u_{k-1}$; show no monochromatic directed cycle exists in $G'$.

nodes.name: $G'$ $k$-dicolourable $\Rightarrow$ $G$ $k$-dicolourable
nodes.statement: Given $\phi$ a $k$-dicolouring of $G'$, the $u_i$ use $k-1$ pairwise distinct colours so $\phi(u^+)=\phi(u^-)$; setting the colour of $u$ to $\phi(u^+)$ yields a valid $k$-dicolouring of $G$.

nodes.name: Forward direction of reduction
nodes.statement: If $G$ is $k$-dicolourable, then $G'$ is too.

nodes.name: Backward direction of reduction
nodes.statement: If $G'$ is $k$-dicolourable, then $G$ is too.

nodes.name: Greedy bound and Mohar's incomplete proof
nodes.statement: Any greedy ordering yields $\vec{\chi}(G) \leq \Delta_{min}(G)+1 \leq \Delta_{max}(G)+1$. The original proof of the directed Brooks' Theorem in [M10] is incomplete because the connectivity of $G \setminus \{v_1, v_2\}$ is not verified.
